scenes.text: Owls can't move their eyes, so they turn their heads instead, up to two hundred seventy degrees.
Their eyes aren't round balls like ours, they're shaped like tubes.
The tubes are locked in place by bone, so the eyes can't roll around.
To make up for it, owls have fourteen neck bones, twice as many as humans.
Scientists at Johns Hopkins found special blood vessels that keep blood flowing while they twist.
If you could spin your head like an owl, what would you look at first?

title: Why owls turn their heads almost all the way around 🦉
caption: Owls' eyes are tube-shaped and fixed in place, so they swivel their heads about 270 degrees instead. They have 14 neck vertebrae, humans have only 7! 🦉
